envelope.text: this CREATES a guard condition into `out` with `callback` bound at

why:
SHIPPED phase-467 Row 8 (2026-09-28). `rclc_node_get_graph_guard_condition(node, out, callback, context)` creates a guard condition the BACKEND triggers when the ROS graph changes, and two backends trigger it: zenoh and Cyclone. Was `gap` + `adopt`; it is `divergence` + `adopt-bounded` now, because the capability arrived and the SHAPE did not become upstream's.

THE ENVELOPE, which is the whole reason this was never one forwarder. `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition(node)` RETURNS a borrowed pointer to a guard the node owns, and upstream's only documented use of that return is `rcl_wait_set_add_guard_condition`. Two PLATFORM constraints rule it out and neither is a preference. (1) There is no allocator at this seam: RFC-0018/0019 makes every entity CALLER STORAGE with the status in the return, so nothing here hands back an owned handle -- the same constraint that shapes `rclc_node_create_guard_condition`, `rclc_publisher_init` and every other creation verb. (2) There is no wait set: RFC-0002 gives each RTOS task ONE executor and `cpp:WaitSet` is declined, so a returned handle would have nowhere to go. So the entry point is upstream's NAME over `rclc_node_create_guard_condition`'s SHAPE, differing from it only in who pulls the trigger -- the application there, the backend's discovery path here. A ported file that tries to put the handle in a wait set fails AT THE WAIT SET, not at this name.

WHAT LANDED, and where the earlier readings were wrong.
  * The ABI slot `nros_rmw_vtable_t::node_get_graph_guard_condition` was declared in phase-376 W4 and had NO trait twin and NO consumer for five phases, which is why the expensive half was never the backends. It has both now: `nros_rmw::Session::set_graph_change_callback` (trait default `Unsupported`), `CffiSession` forwards to the slot, and `rust_adapter.rs` carries a trampoline row -- so the slot is PRODUCED for every Rust backend at once, and a backend with no graph answers `UNSUPPORTED` through the trait default rather than accepting a callback nothing will fire.
  * ZENOH: `zpico_graph_set_apply` has always returned whether the token set CHANGED and `graph_cache_sample_handler` discarded it with a `(void)`. Reading that return is the hook. The five-piece `zpico_set_reply_waker` shape carries it out of C (typedef, per-session field, setter, call site, Rust trampoline), plus the `zpico-sys` extern, its `ffi.rs` no-C stub and a cbindgen regeneration of the committed `zpico.h`. The callback fires OUTSIDE the cache mutex, because the handler it wakes reads the graph.
  * CYCLONE: the phase-467 study said this backend had no change signal at all and recommended splitting the row. It was wrong, as the 2026-09-25 re-read found: the listener is on the PARTICIPANT (`session_set_wake_callback`), DDS propagates an unhandled event up to the parent, and `on_data_available` was throwing the discrimination away in its FIRST PARAMETER. `reader == graph.graph_reader` is the hook. Under `NROS_RMW_CYCLONEDDS_NO_FOREIGN_WAKE` the slot answers `UNSUPPORTED`, for issue 1237's reason measured rather than assumed by analogy: the edge arrives on the same Cyclone receive thread the wake slot declines, and a guard condition trigger ends in the same `nros_platform_wake_signal`.
  * The install/clear pair is the EXECUTOR's, and that is issue 1385's hazard designed out rather than fixed afterwards. The backend never receives a pointer to the caller's `rcl_guard_condition_t`: `Executor::install_graph_change_guard` boxes its OWN `GuardCondition` over the same arena flag, and `clear_graph_change_signal` retires that pointer from the backend BEFORE the box is freed, from `close()` and from `drop`.
  * The capability is PROBED by clearing, before any handle slot is consumed, so an XRCE or uORB caller gets `RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED` and an untouched `out`. Nullity of the vtable slot could not serve as that probe: the Rust adapter fills it for every backend whether or not the backend implements the method, which `check-rmw-slot-producers`'s own report says in as many words.
  * `INERT_FAMILIES["graph-guard"]` is DELETED from `scripts/check-rmw-slot-producers.py`, not reworded -- the slot has a consumer, so it classifies `produced` and a family claiming it would be the stale-claim shape that table checks for. The header's NULL sentence landed in the SAME commit, which is what the gate needs from a slot that becomes reachable.
  * NO `NROS_CODEGEN_VERSION` bump, verified rather than assumed: that surface is what codegen NAMES, and `check-codegen-version-surface.py` reports the same 261 items and version 8 across this change.
  * `docs/reference/rmw-api-map.toml` loses its authored `status = "not-supported"` for this symbol, so the status DERIVES (`re-shaped`) like every other live slot, and RFC-0036's paragraph calling the slot `inert` is corrected in place.

ACCEPTANCE IS A LIVE EDGE, never a produced slot. `graph_interop` gained `a_peer_leaving_fires_the_graph_change_guard` and its Cyclone twin, mapped through `interop::CASE_CELLS` onto the two existing cells `native-graph-rust-{zenoh,cyclone}-r2n` (no new cell: the coordinate did not move, the question did). A stock `demo_nodes_cpp` talker is started, `graph-probe` runs in `GRAPH_PROBE_WATCH_CHANGE` mode until it SEES the talker and latches its edge count, the test kills the talker, and the probe must observe one more edge. A DEPARTURE and not an arrival, because zenoh declares its liveliness subscriber with `history = true` -- an arrival test passes on the start-up burst before any peer has done anything.

That cell earned its keep on the first run. Cyclone armed at 1 -- the arrival HAD fired -- and then reported nothing for thirty seconds after the talker died: a dead participant republishes no `ros_discovery_info`, so that reader never sees another sample. The departure arrives as a DISPOSE on the DDS builtin topics, which the by-topic queries create lazily and this session had never queried. The install now creates all three graph readers (`graph_ensure_reader` + `graph_ensure_builtin_reader`, one creation site each, shared with the queries). Arrivals yes and departures never is WORSE than no edge, because it reads as a working one, and no static check in this tree could have said so.

HISTORY BELOW, kept because it is the reasoning that produced the decisions above.

the guard condition rcl fires when the ROS graph changes. `packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_vtable.h:1162` carries this exact slot, shaped like `set_wake_callback`, precisely so a backend CAN trigger it -- and **no backend fills it.** Measured 2026-09-23: `nullptr` in Cyclone (`packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/vtable.cpp:456`) and uORB (`packages/rmw/uorb/nros-rmw-uorb/src/vtable.cpp:147`), and NULL for zenoh, which does not name the slot anywhere in its vtable construction (`git grep graph_guard_condition -- packages/rmw` hits the ABI header, the generated binding, `EMPTY_VTABLE` and the two C backends, and nothing under `packages/rmw/zenoh`) — so it inherits `EMPTY_VTABLE`'s `None` (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/lib.rs:230`, `:294`). An earlier verdict here said `nothing would ever trigger it`, which is narrower than the truth: nothing triggers it TODAY. NOT impossible -- unimplemented. Phase 379 W3.

**THE FAMILY CLAIM THIS ROW USED TO CARRY IS GONE, BECAUSE IT WAS FALSE.** It said the whole graph family was `None` in the cffi backend with no wrapper or entry point. That stopped being true at phase-381 W4 (eleven entry points in three languages) and phase-444 W3 (Cyclone fills eleven of twelve slots: `get_node_names` at `vtable.cpp:439`, then the ten W3 filled at `:446-455` — `get_{topic,service}_names_and_types`, the four `*_by_node` forms, `get_{publishers,subscriptions}_info_by_topic` and `count_{publishers,subscribers}` — immediately above the one `nullptr`; W3's own comment there says Cyclone "answered UNSUPPORTED to every graph question but `get_node_names`" before it). THIS slot is the twelfth and the only one still empty; deleting the false sentence is the whole change, because the row's own claim survived it intact.

We are VISIBLE in the graph and cannot be NOTIFIED when it changes. Both real backends already run the discovery machinery -- the zenoh shim declares AND queries `@ros2_lv` liveliness tokens (`Ros2Liveliness::*_keyexpr`, wildcard GETs in `shim/session.rs`), the same mechanism `rmw_zenoh_cpp` builds its graph cache from, and `nros-rmw-cyclonedds` publishes `ros_discovery_info` -- so the inputs exist and nothing turns them into an edge.

THIS IS NOT THE WAIT-SET REFUSAL, and it is worth saying because upstream's only documented use of the returned handle is `rcl_wait_set_add_guard_condition`, which we decline at `cpp:WaitSet`. We have a guard condition with a different consumer: `nros::GuardCondition` is a cross-thread wake source whose `trigger()` is lock-free and whose callback runs during `spin_once` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/guard_condition.hpp:34-46`), and the vtable slot is shaped like `set_wake_callback` precisely so a backend can drive one. So the capability has a home here; a ported file that tries to put the handle in a wait set fails at the wait set, not at this name.

ADOPT covers BOTH halves, the way the `*_get_actual_qos` rows do: expose the accessor AND make a backend TRIGGER it. Handing back a guard condition nothing ever fires is the silent-difference shape RFC-0089 Part I exists to refuse. This is the one row in the graph group that is real work rather than a forwarder — it needs graph-CHANGE detection (a zenoh `@ros2_lv` liveliness subscriber, or a Cyclone builtin-topic listener), which is a backend item and not an API one.

RE-READ (phase-444 gap re-read, 2026-09-23) — KEPT `gap` + `adopt`. The row's own claim survived the re-measurement intact; the family sentence around it did not, and is deleted above rather than annotated, because a paragraph that says X over a verdict that says X is false is read in the order it is written.

phase-467 (2026-09-25) — KEPT `gap` + `adopt`, MEASURED, and the study that asked for this measurement got the headline backwards. It recommended SPLITTING this row because "the cost is wildly asymmetric" — zenoh's change signal already arrives, Cyclone "has no change signal at all", so Cyclone's half would be a threading-model change deserving its own issue. **Cyclone has one.** Do not split this row.

WHAT EACH BACKEND DELIVERS TODAY, read 2026-09-25. Both already RECEIVE the edge; both throw away the DISCRIMINATION, in one line each.
  * ZENOH — `zpico_graph_cache_start` declares a STANDING `z_liveliness_declare_subscriber` with `history = true`, so the initial burst and every later token land in `graph_cache_sample_handler` (`packages/rmw/zenoh/zpico-sys/c/zpico/zpico.c`), reached from `ZenohSession::ensure_graph_cache`. That handler calls `zpico_graph_set_apply`, WHICH RETURNS 1 IF THE SET CHANGED — and the handler discards it with `(void)`. The edge is computed already.
  * CYCLONE — the graph READER is created with a `nullptr` listener (`src/graph.cpp`, `dds_create_reader(dds_get_participant(g->topic), …, nullptr)`), which is what the "no change signal" reading saw. But the listener is installed ON THE PARTICIPANT, not per reader: `session_set_wake_callback` does `dds_lset_data_available_arg(…)` + `dds_set_listener(state->participant, …)` (`src/session.cpp`), and its own comment says why — "DDS propagates an unhandled event up to the parent, so one listener covers every reader this session will ever create, including ones created later". `graph_init(&state->graph, pp)` puts the graph topic on that same participant, so a `ros_discovery_info` sample ALREADY wakes `on_data_available` today. What that handler drops is its FIRST PARAMETER: its signature is `on_data_available(dds_entity_t /*reader*/, void *arg)`, and `reader == state->graph.graph_reader` is the whole discriminator.
  * XRCE (issue 2106) — the edge fires when a remote participant's `ros_discovery_info` sample (read through the Agent) changes the node table, or a local node is created or destroyed. It sees no DDS discovery, so a participant leaves the table only by publishing its last, node-less sample on a clean shutdown; measured live (`xrce_ros2_interop::xrce_a_peer_leaving_fires_the_graph_change_guard`: SIGTERM fires it, SIGKILL never does).
  * uORB — no graph, no edge. The answer is `UNSUPPORTED`, which `CffiSession` produces by construction for a `None` slot — but note the HEADER does not say so: unlike `set_wake_callback` two hundred lines above it ("NULL slot = backend has no asynchronous wake path"), this slot's doc block carries no NULL sentence. That is not cosmetic. `check-rmw-slot-producers.py` classifies a REACHABLE slot with no producer and no documented NULL as `unimplemented` and fails, so the sentence has to be written in the same commit that gives the slot a consumer.
Two honest preconditions on the Cyclone side, neither of them a threading change: the participant listener exists only once a wake callback has been installed (every C executor does since issue 1385), and the graph reader is created on FIRST USE of a graph query.

SO THE COST IS NOT ASYMMETRIC — IT IS SHARED, and the shared half is the large one. The two backend hooks are a line each. What is not a line each:
  1. a new `nros_rmw::Session` method (no such method exists today — the ABI slot has never had a trait twin), which recompiles the workspace;
  2. a `CffiSession` forward, and a row in `rust_adapter.rs`'s vtable — note that row makes the slot PRODUCED for every Rust backend at once, so it is not a zenoh-only edit;
  3. the zpico C side of the zenoh hook is FIVE pieces, the shape `zpico_set_reply_waker` already has: fn-pointer typedef, per-session field, setter, call site, Rust trampoline — plus the hand-written `zpico-sys` extern, its `ffi.rs` no-C fallback, and a cbindgen regeneration of the committed `zpico.h`;
  4. an INSTALL/CLEAR PAIR on the executor. This is the part most likely to be skipped and it is issue 1385's hazard exactly: hand the backend a pointer to the caller's `rcl_guard_condition_t` and a `rcl_guard_condition_fini` leaves the backend holding freed storage to call from a worker thread. The executor must own the target and clear it on `close()`/drop, the way `install_wake_signal_on_primary` / `clear_wake_signal` do;
  5. `scripts/check-rmw-slot-producers.py`'s `INERT_FAMILIES["graph-guard"]` must be DELETED, not reworded — the gate fails closed the moment anything reads the slot, and its own precedent for a slot that stops being inert is removal;
  6. a new C entry point means `just regen-c-headers` and the committed `nros_generated.h` diff. It does NOT mean an `NROS_CODEGEN_VERSION` bump: that surface is only what CODEGEN NAMES, and no pack or template names this symbol.
  7. prose that becomes false: `docs/design/0036-ros2-api-divergences.md` says this slot is filled by no backend and classified `inert`, `docs/design/0035-rmw-vtable-abi.md` carries its row, and `book/src/reference/rmw-api-comparison.md` is generated by `scripts/gen-rmw-api-comparison.py`.

THE DECISION THE ROW OWED: THE PRIMITIVE IS RIGHT AND THE VERB IS NOT. The primitive is not in doubt — `nros::GuardCondition` is an arena `AtomicBool` plus a `CallbackMeta` serviced by `guard_try_process` during `spin_once`, `trigger()` is lock-free from any thread, and since issue 1385 a trigger CUTS A PARKED `drive_io` SHORT (measured 400 ms → 51 ms). The vtable slot is already `(session, rmw_event_callback_t, const void *user_data)`, a set-callback. What does not carry is upstream's VERB: `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition` RETURNS a borrowed handle to a guard the node owns, and RFC-0018/0019 forbids returning an owned handle while our guards are created into CALLER storage with their callback bound at creation. So the entry point is `rclc_node_get_graph_guard_condition(node, out, callback, context)` — upstream's NAME over `rclc_node_create_guard_condition`'s SHAPE, differing from it only in who pulls the trigger. That is a stated envelope (`adopt-bounded` on the accessor when it lands), not a silent difference, and it is the reason this row is not "one forwarder".

NOT BUILT IN THIS PASS, and the reason is the list above rather than the two backend lines: it is a `nros-rmw` trait edit, a C ABI-adjacent entry point, a C-side callback in the zenoh shim, an executor-owned install/clear pair, a gate family deletion and two regenerated committed headers — and the backend halves cannot be honestly accepted without a live graph cell on each, which phase-444 W2's router-and-peer lane still owes. What this pass removes is the two things that made the next attempt expensive: the belief that Cyclone needs a threading-model change, and the belief that this is a cheap accessor.
